start.hero-text: See your pensions in one place with our free, secure government-backed service. Plus, see how much you could get when you retire.

section-how-it-works.title: How it works
section-how-it-works.duration: It takes you about **10 minutes** to sign in with GOV.UK One Login, or **25 minutes** if it's your first time.
items: Prove your identity using **GOV.UK One Login**. You can set up an account with One Login as part of this service.
Enter your **National Insurance number**, if you have one. You can still proceed without one.
See all the pensions that match your details, including your estimated income when you retire.

section-you-need.title: You’ll need
items: your current address
your National Insurance number, if you have one
section-you-need.easier: It’s usually easier to prove your identity with GOV.UK One Login if you have:
easier-items: a mobile phone with a working camera
section-you-need.other-ways: But you can prove your identity in other ways. See a full list of [ways to prove your identity with GOV.UK One Login](https://www.gov.uk/using-your-gov-uk-one-login/proving-your-identity).

section-your-data.title: Your data
section-your-data.description: We’ll share the information that you or GOV.UK One Login give us with pension providers, schemes, and the Department for Work and Pensions (DWP) to find your pensions.

more-about-your-data.title: More about how we use your data
items: When we get your information back from pension providers, schemes or the DWP, we store it while you are using the Pensions Dashboard and for up to 30 days after that.
We do securely store some pseudonymised data in order to make the service work. This is when your data is given codes or tokens, so you cannot be directly identified.
Learn more in [our privacy notice_target=_self](/en/dashboard-privacy-notice).

some-pensions-may-not-be-included.title: Some pensions may not be included
some-pensions-may-not-be-included.text: We’re still connecting new pension schemes on a regular basis. However, you will not see pension schemes that:
items: you’ve already taken or you’re receiving money from, including those in pension drawdown
are workplace schemes with fewer than 100 scheme members, unless the provider connects to the Pensions Dashboard voluntarily
are administered outside the United Kingdom
are managed by the Pension Protection Fund (PPF), including the Financial Assistance Scheme (FAS).
some-pensions-may-not-be-included.note-1: You will not see your State Pension if you’ve passed State Pension age, even if you have not claimed it yet.
some-pensions-may-not-be-included.note-2: Providers may not be able to send us information in certain circumstances. In most cases, the Dashboard will provide more details on why this information isn’t showing.

welcome.title: Welcome to the MoneyHelper Pensions Dashboard
welcome.heading: Important information
welcome.intro: Don't make decisions about your money and pensions based solely on the information in your Pensions Dashboard.
welcome.content: The values are for illustration only and are based on some assumptions, such as your retirement age. Always check with your pension providers for the most up-to-date information, and consider speaking to a regulated financial adviser before making decisions about your pensions.

values.title: All pension values:
items: are estimated and not guaranteed
are shown before tax, as pension tax depends on your income and circumstances
could go up or down based on factors such as investment performance and your contributions.

excluded.title: Some information may not be included.
items: You will not see pensions you’ve already taken money from, pensions administered outside the United Kingdom or pensions with very few scheme members.
Providers may not be able to send us information in certain circumstances. In most cases, the Dashboard will provide more details on why this information isn’t showing.

searching-for-your-pension.title: Loading your pensions
searching-for-your-pension.description: This can take up to {duration} seconds. Thanks for your patience.
searching-for-your-pension.refresh: Do not refresh or close this page.

confirmed-pensions.heading: Pensions in your estimate
confirmed-pensions.no-income-link: See pensions [not included_target=_self](#no-income) in your estimate.

confirmed-pensions-no-income.heading: Pensions without estimated incomes
confirmed-pensions-no-income.description:
Some pensions may not display an estimated income, such as pensions less than 2 years from their expected retirement date or schemes in the process of winding up. See the pension’s details for more information.

If any other pensions are missing, see [Pensions not showing_target=_self](/en/pensions-not-showing).

items: Your Pensions Dashboard contains sensitive and valuable information. Think carefully before sharing your information with a third party.
Scammers play on our sense of fear. If you’ve been contacted without warning and told you need to move your pensions to a safe place, this is a scam.

action.heading: If you’re worried about scams, you can:
items: Read our guidance on [spotting pension scams](https://www.moneyhelper.org.uk/en/money-troubles/scams/how-to-spot-a-pension-scam)
Call our Pensions Helpline on [0800 011 3797](tel:08000113797)

onward-journey.heading: Understand your next steps
onward-journey.body: Get free help with your pension, including ways to boost it, how and when you can take an income and if a pension transfer is a good idea.

your-pensions-timeline.title: Your pensions
your-pensions-timeline.heading: Timeline
your-pensions-timeline.intro: The timeline shows how your total estimated pension income could change over time based on each pension’s retirement date
your-pensions-timeline.intro-2: These values are not guaranteed and may go down as well as up.
your-pensions-timeline.intro-3: Your actual income will depend on how and when you take your pensions.

items: These values are based on the pensions we have estimated incomes for so far - they might not include all your pensions. They’re not guaranteed, and may go down as well as up. The incomes and timeline are also based on expected retirement dates from your pension providers. See each pension’s details page for more information.
All values are shown before tax. Learn more about [tax and pensions](/en/support/understand-your-pensions).

headings.income-and-values-sub: These charts show the latest value of your pension sent by your provider, as well as their estimate of what it could be worth in the future.
headings.income-and-values-sub-dc: Your actual income will depend on how and when you take your pension. Learn about your options in our guide, [What can I do with my pension pot?]( https://www.moneyhelper.org.uk/en/pensions-and-retirement/pension-wise/pension-pot-options)

income-and-values.title: About these values
content: The values are based on the calculation date shown below. This is the latest data your pension provider sent us.
Your pension provider might be able to give you a more up-to-date value.

about.title: About these values
about.description: Pension values are based on the latest estimates and expected retirement dates from your pension providers. They’re not guaranteed, and may go down as well as up.
about.sp-description: How much you'll get in your State Pension depends on how many years you've made National Insurance contributions. When you reach State Pension age, you usually need 35 qualifying years to get the full State Pension and 10 qualifying years to get anything. [Learn more](/en/support/understand-your-pensions)

how-estimate-is-calculated.title: How these values are calculated
how-estimate-is-calculated.avc:
Estimates for this pension are based on you buying a guaranteed income for life (an annuity), which starts paying from the expected retirement date. They’re also based on the provider’s assumptions about inflation, investment performance, and future contribution levels.

To help you understand the impact of inflation, the estimated income is shown in today’s money, so you can see what that amount would be worth right now.
how-estimate-is-calculated.dc:
Estimates for this pension are based on you buying a guaranteed income for life (an annuity), which starts paying from the expected retirement date. They’re also based on the provider’s assumptions about inflation, investment performance, and future contribution levels.

To help you understand the impact of inflation, the estimated income is shown in today’s money, so you can see what that amount would be worth right now.

[Contact your provider_target=_self](/en/pension-details/contact-pension-provider) for more details on how they calculate your pension values.
how-estimate-is-calculated.db:
Estimates for this pension are based on your salary and years you’ve been a scheme member, as well as the expected retirement date. They’re also based on the provider’s assumptions about inflation and whether the scheme is active.

To help you understand the impact of inflation, the estimated income is shown in today’s money, so you can see what that amount would be worth right now.
how-estimate-is-calculated.cdc:
Estimates for this pension are based on you getting a one-time lump sum and an income for life that starts paying from the expected retirement date. Your income for life is reviewed and adjusted each year, which means it could go down, as well as up, both before and after you start receiving it. They’re also based on your salary and years you’ve been a scheme member, as well the provider’s assumptions about inflation, investment performance, and future contribution levels.

To help you understand the impact of inflation, the estimated income is shown in today's money, so you can see what that amount would be worth right now.
how-estimate-is-calculated.cb:
Estimates for this pension are based on your salary and years you’ve been a scheme member, as well as the expected retirement date. They’re also based on the provider’s assumptions about inflation and whether the scheme is active.

To help you understand the impact of inflation, the estimated income is shown in today’s money, so you can see what that amount would be worth right now.
how-estimate-is-calculated.missing: The provider has not sent us how they calculated these values.

claiming-your-state-pension.heading: Claiming your State Pension
items: You will not get your State Pension automatically - you have to claim it.
You’ll get a letter no later than 2 months before you reach State Pension age telling you what to do. If you do not get a letter, you can still make a claim.
After you’ve claimed it, it’s paid every **4 weeks** rather than the same date each month.

heading.keep-contributing: You need to keep contributing to reach your forecast
heading.already-qualify: You already qualify for your full forecast amount

text.partial-accrued: You’ve built up enough qualifying years of National Insurance contributions or credits to get some State Pension, but need to keep contributing to reach your forecast amount.
text.full-forecast: You already have enough qualifying years of National Insurance contributions or credits to get your State Pension forecast amount.
text.no-accrued: You usually need at least **10 years** to get any State Pension. You need to keep contributing to qualify for State Pension and reach your forecast amount.

pending-pensions.title: Pending pensions
pending-pensions.description:
**What does 'pending' mean?** Your provider has confirmed the pension is yours. They haven’t sent us all the details yet, so some figures might be missing.

 **Do I need to do anything?** No. Pending pensions will automatically move to ‘Your pensions’ once their information is complete.

pensions-that-need-action.title: Pensions that need action
pensions-that-need-action.tool-intro: You may need to provide more information to confirm whether a pension belongs to you, or there could be another issue the provider needs to speak to you about.

what-you-can-do.heading: What you can do
what-you-can-do.lead: Call, email or write to your provider using the details on this page
what-you-can-do.body-before: Contact your provider using the details on the card and let them know you'd like to resolve an issue with a pension on the MoneyHelper Pensions Dashboard. They might ask you for:
list-items: your full name, plus any previous names
your reference number, if there's one on the card
what-you-can-do.body-after: Once the issue is resolved, the pension will show up in 'Your pensions' or 'Pending pensions'. If it was matched to you by mistake, it will no longer show up on the Pensions Dashboard.

possible-match.heading: Possible match with your details
possible-match.description: The pension provider needs to make sure your information matches their records.

more-information.heading: More information, action or decision needed
more-information.description: The pension provider cannot send any more details until you contact them.

card.description: Contact {pensionAdministrator} and give them your reference number if it’s available.

scam-warning.heading: Beware of scams
scam-warning.description: A pension provider will **never contact you first** to ask for your personal information about a pension they say might belong to you. You must contact the pension provider with your reference number or other identifying details to confirm if a pension is yours.

no-pensions-found.title: No pensions found
no-pensions-found.heading: What you can do:
no-pensions-found.tooltip: We’re still building and improving our service. We’re connecting new pension schemes on a regular basis.

to-do.item-1: Check back later to see if your pensions are showing.
to-do.item-2: Let us know your National Insurance number (NINO) if you haven’t already. You’ll have to sign in again with GOV.UK One Login to return.
to-do.item-2-logout-link: Exit the Pensions Dashboard and start again to enter your National Insurance number.
to-do.item-3: If your State Pension is not showing and you think you’re entitled to one, [check your details using your State Pension forecast](https://www.gov.uk/check-state-pension).
to-do.item-4: If you know the name of your employer(s) or pension provider(s), contact them directly.
to-do.item-5: If you still cannot see your pensions, [report a technical problem](/en/support/report-a-technical-problem).
to-do.item-6: If you had a workplace pension from 1988 or earlier, or if you worked for an employer for less than two years, check if your pension contributions were refunded. [Learn more about refunded pensions.](/en/support/explore-the-pensions-dashboard)

summary-sentence.title: Your estimated income
summary-sentence.state-pension-age: In **{statePensionYear}**, how much could you get from your pensions that year (before tax)?
summary-sentence.annually: This adds up to around **{annualTotal}** a year.
summary-sentence.snapshot: **This is just a snapshot – it doesn't include pensions without an estimated income or that are due to start paying after {statePensionYear}**. As you start or stop taking your pensions, your income may go up or down.
accordion-content: This income is based on the pensions we have estimates for so far - it might not include all your pensions. Pension providers usually update these estimates at least once a year, and make calculations based on each pension’s contribution levels and expected retirement date. They’re not guaranteed, and may go down as well as up. See the pension details for more information.
Most estimated incomes show you how much your pension would be worth in today’s money. All values are shown before tax. Learn more about [tax and pensions](/en/support/understand-your-pensions).
summary-sentence.no-state-pension-1: **You might start taking each of your pensions at different times**. As they start or stop, your income may go up or down.
summary-sentence.no-state-pension-2: To help you see how much money you could have when you retire, we've put the available estimated incomes into a timeline.
summary-sentence.mccloud-accordion-title: Why do I have two options?
mccloud-accordion-content: You have a choice between legacy (final salary) and alternative (career average) pension benefits, which are calculated in different ways. The income and lump sums will be different for each option.
You do not have to choose until you start taking your pension.
summary-sentence.specific-year-accordion-title: Why have we used a specific year?
summary-sentence.specific-year-accordion-content: This is the year you will reach **State Pension age** - the age you can claim your State Pension. You might start taking other pensions before or after this.

pension-detail-next-steps.heading: Understand your next steps
pension-detail-next-steps.intro:
Pensions can be complicated, but we’re here to help you understand your options and next steps. \
Actions you take now might affect how comfortable your retirement is in the future.
pension-detail-next-steps.intro-new-tab: All these links open in a new tab.

cards.title: How can I make the most of my pension?
cards.text: Get free help with your pension, including ways to boost it and how and when you can take an income.

cards.title: How much money will I need in retirement?
cards.text: Find out how much retirement income you’ll need to cover your essential costs with our Budget planner.

cards.title: Will I have enough to live comfortably?
cards.text: See how your estimated retirement income might change if you saved more with our Pension calculator.

cards.title: Should I combine my pensions?
cards.text: If you have multiple pensions, find out if transferring or combining your pensions is a good idea.

tooltips.pension-origin: `tooltip:: The **pension origin** is where this pension scheme comes from, such as a current or former job, a transfer, or an annuity you’ve already bought.::center`
tooltips.retirement-date: `tooltip:: The **pension retirement date** is the date your provider expects you to start taking money from this pension scheme. You don’t have to retire or take your pension on this date - you can usually change it by contacting them.::center`
tooltips.costs-and-charges: `tooltip:: **Costs and charges** are paid to your pension provider to cover the costs of managing your money. They’re usually paid automatically out of your pension scheme.::center`
tooltips.illustration-date: `tooltip:: These values are based on the information your provider had on this specific date. Because information is updated at different times, they might be different from what you see on your annual benefit statements or online account.::`
tooltips.pot-value: `tooltip:: The **pot value** is how much money has built up in this pension scheme. It’s a combination of your contributions, your employer’s contributions (if it’s a workplace pension), and any investment growth.::`
tooltips.lump-sum: `tooltip:: A **lump sum** is a one-time sum of money paid in addition to your pension income, usually when you retire. It’s based on your salary and number of years you’ve been in the pension scheme.::`
tooltips.state-pension-age: `tooltip:: The **State Pension age** is the earliest age you can claim State Pension. You don’t have to start taking your State Pension at this age - you can also defer it.::center`
tooltips.status-active: `tooltip:: If this pension is **active**, you and/or your employer are making contributions (paying into it).::`
tooltips.status-inactive: `tooltip:: If this pension is **inactive**, it’s no longer being paid into but your money is still being managed by the pension provider.::`
tooltips.linked-pension: `tooltip:: A pension is **linked** when the pension's benefits come from more than one pension provider or scheme.::`
tooltips.type-AVC: `tooltip::An **AVC (additional voluntary contributions) scheme** is a separate pension pot you pay into on top of your regular workplace pension contributions. AVCs can be managed by the same pension provider as your workplace pension or separately.::`
tooltips.type-DB: `tooltip::A **defined benefit** pension is a workplace pension where your income is based on your salary and years you've been a scheme member. [Learn more](/en/support/understand-your-pensions)::`
tooltips.type-DC: `tooltip::A **defined contribution** pension is a pot of money that you (and sometimes your employer) pay into for your retirement. It’s an investment, so your income depends on the investment’s performance and how you choose to take your pension at retirement. [Learn more](/en/support/understand-your-pensions)::`
tooltips.type-HYB: `tooltip::A **hybrid pension** is a scheme with both defined benefit and defined contribution features. Depending on the scheme, you could either get a combination of these types of incomes or the higher of the two.::`
tooltips.type-CDC: `tooltip::A **collective defined contribution (CDC)** scheme pays you a regular income for life when you retire. The income can rise or fall before and after you start taking it. This depends on many factors, like how well the scheme’s investments have performed. Your money is invested together with the contributions from your employer and other scheme members, so the risk is shared and the pension might grow at a higher rate. [Learn more](/en/support/understand-your-pensions)::`
tooltips.type-CB: `tooltip::A **cash balance** scheme is a workplace pension where the employer guarantees either a lump sum at retirement or that contributions grow at a guaranteed rate for each year you work. They also take responsibility for the investment risk, which means you’ll know the value of your pension pot when you decide to access it. [Learn more](/en/support/understand-your-pensions)::`
tooltips.type-CBLUMP: `tooltip::This **cash balance lump sum** is a guaranteed amount of money when you retire. You can choose how to take it, for example by buying an annuity (a guaranteed regular income) or by choosing more flexible income options.::`
tooltips.type-VAR: `tooltip::This pension includes a **combination** of benefit types. These can be calculated in different ways, have separate incomes and be paid out at different times.::`
tooltips.national-insurance: `tooltip:: **National Insurance (NI)** is a type of tax you pay to qualify for State Pension and some types of benefits. You usually need 35 qualifying years of NI contributions to get the full State Pension and 10 qualifying years to get anything. [Learn more](/en/support/understand-your-pensions)::`
